notes: Override of AbstractProceduralTextureNode.method3049/readProperty (see refactor-notes/commonMain/AbstractProceduralTextureNode.csv; tag expected to be 31015 at real call sites, per ProceduralTextureGraph's node-decode loop). Handles only fieldId==0: reads the curve interpolation type anInt9211 (0=linear, 1=eased, 2=cubic -- see buildCurveLookupTable/method3081) from a byte at a fixed buffer offset, then reads a control-point count and populates anIntArrayArray9210 with that many (x,y) marker pairs (the curve's control points/knots). The `if (tag==31015) anInt9213++` at the end is a plain counter, not a real gate -- it matches the base class's documented tag convention and is true at every real call site.

Private helper, called once from prepareLookupTables/method3044 as `buildCurveLookupTable(-1)`. Builds the 257-entry output lookup table aShortArray9215 (indexed 0..256, covering the 0..4096 fixed-point input domain in 16-unit steps) by interpolating between the control points in anIntArrayArray9210, using one of 3 schemes selected by the curve type anInt9211: 2 = cubic (4-point weighted interpolation using getMarkerAt/method3083 to fetch/extrapolate the two surrounding and two outer neighbour points), 1 = eased (uses a precomputed ease/S-curve table, WidgetComponentNode.anIntArray4654, to blend between the two bracketing points), and the fallback/default (0 or any other value) = plain linear interpolation between the two bracketing points. Every output sample is clamped to the Short range (-32767..32767). The `unused` param only gates `if (unused != -1) aShortArray9215 = null` at the very end -- dead at the only real call site, which always passes -1.

Override of AbstractProceduralTextureNode.method3042/getMonochromeRow (tag expected 255, per the base class CSV; checked here via `if (tag != 255) anIntArray9214 = null`, a decoy branch since real callers always use tag=255). Fetches/allocates the row cache via aSpriteSheetCache_7032.method1433(0, row); when freshly dirty, pulls the input node's row via getInputMonoOrRedRow/method3048(row, 633706337, 0), and for each pixel maps the input sample (shr 4, clamped to 0..256) through the baked curve lookup table aShortArray9215 to produce the output value. This is the actual 'apply the curve/gradient remap to an input signal' operation that gives the class its name -- effectively a levels/curves-style remap node.

Private helper, called only from prepareLookupTables/method3044 when the curve type is cubic (anInt9211==2), as `computeExtrapolatedMarkers(73.toByte())`. Computes two synthetic 'virtual' control points beyond the real marker list's ends -- one extrapolated from the last two real markers (stored in anIntArray9208) and one extrapolated from the first two real markers (stored in anIntArray9214) -- so the 4-point cubic interpolation in buildCurveLookupTable/method3081 has usable neighbour points even for segments adjacent to the first/last real marker. The `unused` param only gates a decoy call `if (unused.toInt() != 73) getMonochromeRow(75, 39)`, which never fires since the only real call site passes 73.toByte().

Override of AbstractProceduralTextureNode.method3044/prepareLookupTables (loadTag expected 120 at the real call site, per the base class CSV). Defaults anIntArrayArray9210 to a 2-point identity curve (intArrayOf(0,0) -> intArrayOf(4096,4096)) if no markers were decoded; the `if (loadTag<=108) anIntArrayArray9210 = null` branch is dead at the real call site (120>108). Throws if fewer than 2 markers exist ('Curve operation requires at least two markers'). If the curve type is cubic, first computes the boundary extrapolation via computeExtrapolatedMarkers/method3082, then always calls buildCurveLookupTable/method3081(-1) to bake the final 257-entry output LUT. Also calls TrigLookupInit.method1605(26188), presumably to ensure a shared trig/ease lookup table this node depends on is initialized.

Private indexed accessor over the control-point list anIntArrayArray9210, used by buildCurveLookupTable/method3081 to fetch a marker at `index-2`/`index+1` for cubic interpolation. Returns the synthetic 'before first' extrapolated marker anIntArray9214 when `index<0`, the synthetic 'after last' extrapolated marker anIntArray9208 when `index>=` the marker count, and otherwise the real marker anIntArrayArray9210[index] -- effectively a clamped/extrapolated marker lookup so cubic interpolation never indexes out of bounds. The `unused` Byte param is only used in a discarded computation (`-48 % ((unused - 13) / 56)`) -- decoy.
